reader.decision: Approve the batch endpoint (POST /v2/contacts:batchUpsert) with a small Retry-After retry guard. Backoff alone is rejected. I will get a sample batchUpsert response so the per-contact result handling can be coded.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the limit is 100 requests per minute and the job needs 468 minutes of that, so backoff cannot fix throughput. Batching cuts the job to 468 calls, about 6 minutes, with no contract change. The enterprise tier costs 1,450 USD per month and its 3-week lead time misses Friday.

reconstruction.problem: The nightly sync sends one PUT per contact. After the Fairhaven import there are 46,800 changed contacts, and Juniper allows only 100 requests per minute per API key. The 8 workers send about 400 per minute, so about 300 get 429.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Only about 100 contacts per minute succeed, and failures skip mark_synced. The 7200 s deadline caps the job at 12,000 contacts (11,940 in the log), leaving 34,860 pending. Those Fairhaven leads miss the Friday 09:00 UTC campaign start in TS-77. The two November imports of about 40,000 would also need about 8 hours each. Backoff only removes the 429 noise, not the throughput limit.
reconstruction.fix: Add batch_upsert_contacts in sync/crm_client.py, posting to contacts:batchUpsert at 100 contacts per request, with a Retry-After sleep and a few retries on 429. Change sync_one in sync/run_sync.py to take a chunk of 100 and call mark_synced only for contacts that succeeded. Failed contacts stay unsynced for the next night. Bump the image tag in deploy/cron.yaml from 2026.10.3 to the new release. The job then makes 468 calls in about 6 minutes, under the limit.
reconstruction.cost: About ten lines for the Retry-After guard, plus changes to three files and a release that must ship before 01:00 UTC on 29 October. The risk is that docs/juniper-api.md gives no field names for per-contact results, so a sample response is needed. The fallback, the enterprise tier, costs 1,450 USD per month with a 3-week lead time.

follow_up_questions: Can you get a sample batchUpsert response showing a succeeded and a failed contact, so the result handling can be coded?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve the batch endpoint with the Retry-After guard. I will get a sample batchUpsert response from Juniper, for example from their support or a test call in a sandbox, and send it to you. I can't share one from the message, which doesn't contain one.
